_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Single-user lists have no participant filter. The browser's requests carry the header X-ExeDev-Email: me@example.com, so the current user is me@example.com. The test harness has already stubbed the server's conversation list and cut off its live update stream, so there is nothing to set up, intercept or check about that (do not look at the API): the drawer (".drawer") shows the conversations the test names, as rows [data-conversation-id="<id>"] whose title (".conversation-title") is their slug, which is their id (drafts have none), and whose preview is "Preview". The list is "mine" (written in by me@example.com alone), its subagent "subagent" (written in by other@example.com), and "draft" (a draft). "The search toggle" is the button "Search conversations...". Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is {"role": "button", "name": "X", "exact": true}, with a "selector" to scope it when it is a row's, a menu's or a group's; but "there is no button X" counts {"role": "button", "name": "X"} without exact, so that a name containing X counts too. Texts that "are exactly [...]" are checked with assert_texts. "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. 1. Navigate to /new. 2. There is no ".drawer-search-input". 3. The search toggle does not have the class "search-toggle-active". 4. There is no ".conversation-participant-badge". 5. [data-conversation-id="mine"] and [data-conversation-id="draft"] are visible. 6. Click the search toggle. 7. There is no button "Add user filter".
